$comment: Whether to log in, how, and what to say when we cannot. Read by tests/shared/saslplan.test.ts and the Android SharedCorpusTest. The two clients disagreed quietly: the phone authenticated whenever a password was saved and defaulted to PLAIN, the desktop only when a mechanism had been picked and never checked there was a password. One config logged in on one device and sat there as a stranger on the other, with no message on either.
$cases: `config` is the network's SASL settings; `offered` is what the server advertised, or null where it named none. `action` is one of authenticate, skip or refuse; `mechanism` and `reason` go with those.

cases.name: a username and a password, and nothing chosen, is PLAIN
the same with no server list to check against
a chosen mechanism is used as chosen
and is matched however it was typed
nothing set up at all is not an error
a username with no password is still nothing to send
a mechanism chosen with no password says so
cases.reason: SASL PLAIN needs a password, and this network has none saved.

cases.name: EXTERNAL uses the certificate rather than a password
EXTERNAL without one says which is missing
cases.reason: SASL EXTERNAL needs a client certificate, and this network has none set up.

cases.name: a mechanism the server will not take, named with what it will
cases.reason: This server does not offer SCRAM-SHA-512. It accepts PLAIN, SCRAM-SHA-256.

cases.name: an empty list from the server is no list, not an empty one
a password that cannot be read is not a password
cases.reason: Your saved password for this network could not be read — it was encrypted by a keyring this computer no longer has. Enter it again in the network settings.

$accounts: Who we authenticate as: the account name where there is one, and the nick otherwise.

accounts.name: and the nick stands in when there is none
a blank account name is no account name
